title: Choose the default Workers AI model for cloud runs: inventory, price, benchmarks
description:
The factory currently routes [orchestrator].model at workers-ai/@cf/openai/gpt-oss-120b — a placeholder picked because it was visible in the model list, not because it was chosen. Decide the default deliberately.

Three things to establish, in this order:
1. INVENTORY. Enumerate what Workers AI actually serves today on this account (GET /accounts/<id>/ai/models/search — the operator token already has ai read access). Record model id, context window, and whether it speaks the OpenAI-compatible shape the pi/omp kinds need. Do not work from memory or blog posts: the list moves, and this repo has been burned twice this epic by assuming platform behaviour.
2. PRICE. Workers AI bills per neuron/token; capture the actual unit price per model and convert to a comparable per-million-token figure. The point of the Workers AI rung is that inference bills to the same prepaid Cloudflare pool as compute and storage, so the comparison that matters is cost-per-completed-tick, not headline rate.
3. CAPABILITY. Compare against coding-agent benchmarks — DeepSWE and SWE-bench-family scores are the relevant ones for a harness that edits code and runs tests, far more than chat leaderboards. An orchestrator model that cannot reliably drive tool calls is worthless here regardless of price.

Operator-suggested candidates to evaluate (verify availability rather than assuming): the Qwen 3.x family, the DeepSeek families, and Kimi K3 if and when Workers AI serves it. gpt-oss-120b is the incumbent and must be in the comparison as the baseline it is.

Deliverable: a recommendation per ROLE/TIER rather than one global default — the orchestrator drives the skill loop and needs tool-use reliability, while economy implementers can trade capability for price. Say plainly where a Workers AI model is NOT good enough and a BYOK frontier model should stay in the table; the design explicitly expects a mixed routing, and a recommendation that pretends otherwise would be worse than none.

Pairs with kuf: that tick measures container start cost, this one measures inference cost. Together they price a wave.
notes:
2026-08-20 17:08 - EVIDENCE FROM A LIVE RUN (2026-08-20), and it makes this tick decisive rather than exploratory. run_5c3d7e4f booted perfectly on workers-ai/@cf/openai/gpt-oss-120b — model probe green, harness probe green, omp answered READY — and was given the correct prompt: 'continue the ticks skill's orchestrator loop to the end of epic 72y: waves, spawn, wait, collect, merge, integrated gate, close, review, closeout'.

It produced 271 bytes. It stated the resolved substrate, quoted the tk note it would record, and stopped. One turn. It did not enter the wave loop. Cost /bin/zsh.22.

So gpt-oss-120b reasons correctly and CAN call tools (xrz proved that separately) but does not SUSTAIN a long tool-using orchestration loop. That is precisely the capability this tick exists to measure, and it is why the recommendation must be per role: an orchestrator that stops after one turn is useless regardless of price, while the same model may be fine for a well-specified economy implementer.

Add to this tick's method: benchmark scores are a proxy — the decisive test for the ORCHESTRATOR role is whether the model completes a multi-wave loop end to end. Include that as an acceptance check for whichever model is recommended for [orchestrator].model.
2026-08-20 17:18 - LIVE INVENTORY from the operator's account (2026-08-20, GET /accounts/<id>/ai/models/search, 64 models). All three operator-named families ARE served — this tick no longer needs to establish availability, only price and capability:

  DeepSeek v4:  @cf/deepseek-ai/deepseek-v4-pro-0813
                @cf/deepseek-ai/deepseek-v4-flash-0731
                @cf/deepseek-ai/deepseek-r1-distill-qwen-32b
  Kimi:         @cf/moonshotai/kimi-k2.7-code   (a CODE variant — likely the most relevant single entry here)
                @cf/moonshotai/kimi-k2.6
  Qwen:         @cf/qwen/qwen3.8-27b
                @cf/qwen/qwen2.5-coder-32b-instruct
                @cf/qwen/qwen3-30b-a3b-fp8, @cf/qwen/qwq-32b
  Incumbent:    @cf/openai/gpt-oss-120b, @cf/openai/gpt-oss-20b
  Also:         @cf/meta/llama-4-scout-17b-16e-instruct, @cf/mistralai/mistral-small-3.1-24b-instruct

Operator judgement, recorded: the DeepSeek v4 family is expected to be substantially stronger than the gpt-oss incumbent. kimi-k2.7-code and qwen2.5-coder-32b-instruct are the other code-specialised entries and belong in the comparison for the IMPLEMENT roles even if not for the orchestrator.

Note the pro/flash split maps naturally onto the tier vocabulary this repo already uses — pro for orchestrator and strong, flash for economy — which is the shape the recommendation should probably take rather than one global default.
acceptance_criteria: A committed comparison table of the Workers AI models actually available, with id, context window, OpenAI-compatibility, unit price and a per-million-token figure, alongside DeepSWE/SWE-bench-family scores where published; an explicit recommended model per role and tier with the reasoning; and a stated position on which roles should stay on a BYOK frontier model. Availability and prices are dated and sourced from the live API, not from memory.
